topics.title: Physical properties of metals and non-metals

concepts.learning_objective: Describe lustre, hardness, malleability, ductility, conduction of heat and electricity and sonority of metals and relate them to uses.
Identify the physical properties of non-metals and the exceptions that make physical properties alone insufficient for classification.

topics.title: Reactions of metals with oxygen, water and acids

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how metals form oxides with oxygen, including basic and amphoteric oxides and protective oxide layers.
Compare the reactions of metals with cold water, hot water and steam and write the products formed.
Explain the reactions of metals with dilute acids, including the special behaviour of nitric acid.

topics.title: Displacement reactions and the reactivity series

concepts.learning_objective: Predict whether a metal will displace another metal from its salt solution.
Use the reactivity series and displacement results to arrange metals in order of reactivity.
Show the formation of ionic compounds by transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal.
Explain the physical nature, melting points, solubility and electrical conduction of ionic compounds.
Define minerals, ores and gangue and relate the occurrence of metals to their reactivity.
Distinguish roasting from calcination and outline how metals of medium reactivity are extracted.
Choose a suitable reduction method (heat, carbon, displacement or electrolysis) from a metal's place in the activity series.
Describe electrolytic refining, including the electrodes, the electrolyte and the fate of impurities.
Identify the conditions needed for iron to rust from an experiment.
Explain methods of preventing rusting, such as painting and galvanisation.
Explain what alloys are and how alloying changes the properties of metals.
